# Code review: STEP 1 backend auth/DI

## Verdict: PASS

STEP 1 is functionally complete and correct. I found no blocking defect in its authentication, CORS, or DI changes.

The full build remains red solely because of the pre-existing STEP 3 `QualityReceipt` mismatch. Git blame confirms both the invalid property writes and current model originated in the initial commit; STEP 1 did not introduce them.

Runtime 401/CORS requests cannot be executed until that compile failure is resolved, so those criteria were independently verified by static control-flow review rather than an HTTP smoke test.

## Findings

No functional STEP 1 defects.

Two non-blocking hygiene findings:

- [step1-backend-auth-di.md](D:/vault/SM/CourseDeveloperStudio/docs/tickets/handoffs/step1-backend-auth-di.md:9) — “Files touched” lists only the two API files, although the change also touches the Infrastructure project and two source files. The later verification section explains them, but the opening inventory is incomplete.
- [FrontmatterEnvelopeParser.cs](D:/vault/SM/CourseDeveloperStudio/backend/src/CourseDeveloper.Infrastructure/Obsidian/FrontmatterEnvelopeParser.cs:34) — the semantic fix is exactly right, but line-ending normalization makes Git report nearly the entire file as changed (`58 insertions, 59 deletions`). With end-of-line differences ignored, only the intended `TrimStart('\r', '\n')` correction remains.

## Verification results

- SDK installed: .NET SDK `9.0.317`, runtime `9.0.19`.
- `dotnet` is absent from this process’s `PATH`, but invoking `C:\Program Files\dotnet\dotnet.exe` directly works.
- JWT configuration is correct:
  - Live discovery reports issuer `https://gjxhfyfonjdcaimxjipp.supabase.co/auth/v1`.
  - Its JWKS currently contains an ES256 verification key.
  - `Authority`, `ValidIssuer`, audience `authenticated`, signing-key, lifetime, and issuer validation are correctly configured.
  - No static JWT secret remains.
  - `UseAuthentication()` correctly precedes `UseAuthorization()`.
  - The fallback policy protects all controller endpoints; no controller has `[AllowAnonymous]`.
- CORS uses a trimmed explicit origin list. The localhost default is restrictive and production must configure known origins.
- `UseCors` placement before authentication/authorization is correct.
- Changing both coordinators to scoped is correct because they consume scoped repositories. The singleton `NpgsqlDataSource` and `ObsidianVaultService` do not create captive dependencies.
- Both syntax repairs preserve the evident intended behavior:
  - Escaped JSON quotes in `McpToolDispatcher`.
  - Removal of CR/LF characters from the frontmatter body prefix.
- Adding `Npgsql` to Infrastructure is necessary because that project directly compiles against Npgsql types.
